title: OpenAI explains the storage platform serving more than one billion weekly users
friendlyTitle: How OpenAI stores data for more than one billion users
summary: OpenAI says its Habitat storage platform now handles more than 70 million requests per second and over 500 petabytes of data across almost 40 regions. The company also reports that two engineers, assisted by Codex and GPT-5.5, rewrote the service from Python to Rust, improving CPU and memory efficiency.
friendlySummary: OpenAI shared how its storage system supports ChatGPT and other products. It says the system handles huge amounts of data and traffic across many regions.
whyItMatters: The account shows that dependable AI products still rest on conventional engineering: storage, access controls, observability and careful migrations. It also offers a concrete example of coding agents accelerating a large rewrite without removing the need for measured production validation.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Fast AI also needs reliable databases and careful engineering. AI helped with a major code rewrite, but people still checked the new system in production.
